[RAOT.9.5] **No byte of a `CompiledCode` atom is mapped, populated or made executable
until the artefact has verified.** `dsc_sha256` ([RDSC.3.6]) and the
dialect/realtime bindings ([RBND.5]) MUST both have passed before the loader
performs any step of [RAOT.3.4] — before the `mmap`, not merely before the
`mprotect`.

This is the one ordering in the corpus whose violation is a security
consequence rather than a behavioural one. Loading a `CompiledCode` atom maps bytes out of
the artefact as executable memory, so a `.dsc` is an arbitrary-code-execution
surface and not merely a data file. [RDSC.9.1] and [RDSC.9.3] describe a single
forward pass dispatching each atom to its handler as it is read, and [RAOT.9.1]
says the loader processes `CompiledCode` atoms in stream order — so a conforming reading
of those clauses alone maps and `mprotect`s attacker-controlled bytes *during*
the pass and verifies the digest when the stream ends, by which point the pages
are executable in the process's address space whether or not anything calls
them.

[RDSC.9.8]'s "on any load error, the engine's state must be unchanged" does not
cover it: a page already mapped is not engine state, and unmapping it afterwards
is not the same property.

Verification is whole-artefact and `CompiledCode` atoms are per-node, so this ordering
constrains the LOADER's structure and not the stream's: the digest cannot be
checked until the last byte is read, therefore no `CompiledCode` atom may be acted on
during the reading pass. A loader that stages `CompiledCode` bodies and applies them after
verification satisfies it; one that acts on them in stream order does not,
whatever order the atoms appear in.
